title: Leave the book untouched when the accrual fails

blocks.text: This practice continues the interest accrual: `Accrual.java` here is the finished version of the previous practice, with `Adjust` working as you wrote it.

Last month one account held a corrupt negative balance, the adjustment threw on it, and the accrual failed. The operator fixed the account and ran the accrual again, and thousands of customers were paid two months of interest. The bank wants the accrual to be all or nothing.

items: a book with no bad account is adjusted as before;
when any adjustment fails, `accrue()` fails with that exception, and the array the caller passed holds exactly what it held before the call, then and afterwards.

blocks.text: About four lines in total. One test holds part of the accrual until after the failure has reached the caller.

cases.says: a book with no bad account is adjusted, every balance once, for any size and threshold
when an adjustment fails, balances adjusted before the failure are not left changed
a failed adjustment reaches the caller of accrue() as its exception, rather than the accrual returning as if it had run
a part of the accrual that is still running when the failure reaches the caller cannot change the book afterwards

origin.section: A Failure Leaves the Array Partly Changed, So Write to a Copy

concepts: When a leaf throws, invoke() rethrows but every leaf that ran keeps its writes, so the array is left partly changed.
invokeAll rethrows a failure without waiting for a subtask already running, which keeps writing after the caller has caught the exception, so a rollback in the catch can be overwritten.
Running the action on a copy and publishing it only when invoke() returns normally leaves the original untouched on failure.
